record.original_question: For orthogonal term-rewriting systems, is the decision problem for strong sequentiality NP-complete?

evidence.quote: Is the decidability of strong sequentiality for orthogonal term rewriting systems NP-complete?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A term-rewriting system (TRS) consists of a signature of function symbols (each with a fixed arity), a countable set of variables, and a finite set of rewrite rules l → r, where l and r are terms built from the signature and variables, l is not a variable, and every variable occurring in r also occurs in l. A TRS is left-linear if no variable occurs more than once in any left-hand side l. Two rules l₁ → r₁ and l₂ → r₂ (renamed apart) are said to overlap if there is a non-variable position p in l₁ such that l₁|_p and l₂ unify, except for the trivial overlap of a rule with itself at the root position. A TRS is orthogonal if it is left-linear and has no overlaps.

Let Ω be a fresh constant symbol denoting "unknown". Define a partial order ⊑ on terms over the extended signature by Ω ⊑ t for every term t, and f(s₁,…,s_n) ⊑ f(t₁,…,t_n) whenever s_i ⊑ t_i for all i. A position p in a term t (with t|_p = Ω) is called an index of t (with respect to a TRS R) if every term t' with t ⊑ t' that is a redex of R (i.e., matches some left-hand side at the root) has t'|_p ≠ Ω. A redex scheme is a left-hand side with all variables replaced by Ω. An orthogonal TRS R is called strongly sequential if every term t containing Ω that has a redex above it in some reduct admits an index, where indices are computed using the redex schemes only (a syntactic, decidable approximation due to Huet and Lévy).

The decision problem STRONG-SEQUENTIALITY takes as input a finite orthogonal TRS R and asks whether R is strongly sequential. This problem is known to be decidable.

Question. Determine whether STRONG-SEQUENTIALITY for orthogonal term-rewriting systems is NP-complete.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact complexity classification of deciding strong sequentiality for orthogonal term rewriting systems is listed among the RTA List of Open Problems. While decidability is known (Huet-Lévy) and certain related variants admit EXPTIME algorithms, no published result establishes NP-completeness (or rules it out). The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Sequentiality in orthogonal term rewriting systems - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Huet and Lévy introduced strongly sequential TRSs and showed strong sequentiality is decidable for orthogonal TRSs.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability is established but precise complexity bounds (NP-completeness) are not given.
